label: first token is v/m; or second copy step in very short sequences
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) Sequence start: at t=0 when the input is v or m. This fires every time (dev precision 1.0) but always weakly (about 0.05-0.06 of max), and makes up 57% of activations but only 32% of mass. It also fires weakly on v/m at later original positions. (2) Copy phase at recall_idx==1 (step L+1, where orig(0) is fed back and orig(1) is output), only in short sequences: L=3 fires about 45% of the time, L=4 about 10%, and L>=5 almost never. This component holds all the strongest activations (up to max) and 56% of the mass. Magnitude depends weakly on which tokens are involved (fed-back v/x/s/d and output e/b/t are over-represented at the top), but no token set separates active from inactive. Widening to L<=4 raises dev mass recall from 0.62 to 0.87 but drops precision to 0.40. Never fires on the delimiter step, on any other copy step, or at original positions >=4.
